This is an RCT (35 subjects randomly assigned) comparing methylphenidate and Adderall with a lactose placebo control in teenagers with ADHD. The study includes MPH vs placebo comparisons. Age criterion met (teenagers). IQ information not reported in abstract - conservatively including pending full text verification.

While this study uses a placebo-controlled double-blind design with methylphenidate, the population consists of adolescents with comorbid aggressive conduct disorder AND ADHD, not pure ADHD. The primary outcome measured is aggression (Adolescent Antisocial Behavior Checklist), not ADHD symptoms. Very small sample (n=9 total, only 6 in double-blind phase). Does not meet the population criterion for children/adolescents with ADHD as the primary condition.

This study examines methylphenidate AUGMENTATION to atomoxetine, not methylphenidate monotherapy vs placebo. All participants received atomoxetine (1.2 mg/kg/day) plus either methylphenidate or placebo augmentation. This does not meet the selection criterion of 'methylphenidate versus placebo or no intervention' as the comparison is between two active drug combinations (atomoxetine+MPH vs atomoxetine+placebo).

This is an RCT comparing methylphenidate (5mg and 15mg twice daily) versus placebo in 57 students with ADHD. The study measures behavioral ratings in school situations. Age criterion likely met (school students). IQ information not reported in abstract - conservatively including pending full text verification.

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover RCT comparing Ritalin (methylphenidate) and Adderall with placebo in 25 children with ADHD (mean age 9.6 years). The study explicitly states participants were 'of average intelligence', suggesting normal IQ. Meets all three selection criteria: RCT design, MPH vs placebo comparison, children with ADHD, and likely normal IQ population.

This is an RCT (randomized into MPH and placebo for 7 days each in crossover design) in 36 boys with ADHD aged 8.3-9.7 years. The study compares methylphenidate versus placebo. Age criterion met. IQ information not reported in abstract - conservatively including pending full text verification.

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover RCT administering methylphenidate to 14 children with ADD+H (ADHD). The study compares multiple doses of methylphenidate versus placebo. Age criterion likely met (children). IQ information not reported in abstract - conservatively including pending full text verification.

This is NOT a primary research study or RCT. It is a commentary/critique paper discussing errors and misinterpretations in a Cochrane systematic review. It does not present original data from a randomized clinical trial comparing methylphenidate versus placebo. Clearly does not meet any of the selection criteria.

This study does not appear to be a randomized controlled trial. The abstract describes observations of unmedicated children with ADHD during a go/no-go task and reports that 'methylphenidate reverted the level of mind blanking to baseline' but does not describe randomization, placebo control, or a proper RCT design. The second experiment involved adults with subclinical ADHD, which would not meet the age criterion anyway. Does not meet the RCT design criterion.
